newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia to launch second-tier shares trading system. [CORRECTED 17:00 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Russia to launch second-tier shares trading system. [CORRECTED 17:00 GMT]

text.p: Russia will launch a trading system dedicated to less liquid, second-tier shares on December 15, the National Association of Stock Market Participants (NAUFOR) said on Friday.
The system, Russian Trading System-2 (RTS-2), complements the Russian Trading System (RTS), which is Russia's equivalent to NASDAQ and accounts for most of domestic trading volume.

NAUFOR national listing committee executive director Alexander Kuzetenko told Reuters that officials were in the process of selecting several dozen shares to be traded on the new screen-based system, mostly shares of regional telecommunications and utilities firms.
RTS trades shares in 85 companies, of which 24 are leading firms which comprise the RTS daily index.
Some second-tier telecoms and utilities are a favourite with foreign investors, who say the companies are undervalued and have attractive price-earnings ratios.
A NAUFOR statement said companies must have at least five billion roubles in shareholders' funds to be listed on RTS-2.
To be listed on RTS, companies must have a market capitalisation of at least $5 million.
The minimum lot of shares one can trade on RTS-2 lot must total five million roubles, compared to $5,000 on RTS.
Brokers on RTS-2 can supply bids or offers, while brokers on RTS must supply both.
RTS-2 trading will be in roubles -- unlike RTS, where trading is done in dollars.
RTS-2 will have no daily fluctuation limit for best bids and offers, compared to RTS, where the limit is 10 percent.
